recipes.name: Kid-Approved Sweet and Sour Chicken Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) can pineapple, drained and juice reserved
0.25 cup white vinegar or apple cider vinegar

steps.text: Stir reserved pineapple juice, sugar, ketchup, and vinegar in a saucepan over medium heat until blended, 2 to 3 minutes.
Whisk water and cornstarch in a bowl until cornstarch is dissolved; stir into pineapple juice mixture.
Stir pineapple and carrots into the sauce; bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook at a simmer until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Kid-Approved Sweet and Sour Chicken Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy sweet and sour dipping sauce goes perfectly with chicken nuggets and white rice and is kid-tested and approved. Simple and tasty!

review.reviewBody: I wrote this recipe! PLEASE disregard the vinegar! You can use vinegar or ketchup, but not both! Also, you can use orange/ lemon lime soda or ginger ale instead of pineapple juice and water. Cut the sugar way down if you use soda. It is also fantastic with brown sugar and/ or soy sauce. I make this almost daily. (with whatever combo of ingredients I have on hand).The recipe is so forgiving and it will whip up in a sauce pan in no time. . My kids dip everything in it!

Was super great!! I did the vinegar version with just a touch of ketchup for color. I added to chicken drumsticks that I dipped in egg mixture with pepper and homemade chilli sauce, and then dipped in flour with red pepper, black pepper, paprika and cayenne. I baked the chicken at 375 for an hour (pan rubbed with olive oil and pam)and flipped chicken once. then i scooped sauce into the chicken glass pan and let bake for another 10 minutes then turned it super down for another 10 mintutes. then i covered it until my hubby got home and was a super yummy success served over white rice. yeh! thanks a bunch!!

This was a very quick and easy recipe. Changes I made were to reduce the sugar to only 3 tablespoons. I also used only 1/2 of the ketchup and used Thai sweet chili sauce for the remaining amount. That added a nice kick without overwhelming. I used rice vinegar, but feel that it needed the stronger flavor of apple cider vinegar.
Loved it but I substituted the pineapple juice with two tablespoons of honey and it came out 🔥

I was very skeptical of this recipe. I followed the notes to switch leave out the vinegar and substitute lemon-lime soda for the pineapple. This came out very well. I added a bit of soy sauce, brown sugar and a touch of barbeque sauce. My kids loved it and it is way better than any of the bottled stuff in the grocery store. The novelty of ketchup and soda mixed together helped too I think. I will use it again when I need a sweet and sour sauce.

Will be using this as my go to recipe for sweet and sour sauce. I did reduce the sugar to 1/2 cup instead of the 1 cup and found it was sweet enough. My girls frowned upon me putting the pineapple back into the pan so I did leave them out (they came in asking what was for supper and saw the pineapple sitting out and asked why). Hubby said it had good flavor but could be a bit more tangier so next time I think I'll add a bit more vinegar.(I also did not add the optional carrots) Thanks for the recipe! AAA+++

Luckily, I read the comment about choosing ketchup OR vinegar and not doing both! That would have wasted time and money had I not happened to read that. I would also suggest using a little bit less sugar. I went the ketchup route, so maybe the vinegar wouldn’t be this way, but it was just a little bit too sweet, even for for my kids. I’m also adding some onions and bell peppers next time because it was all kind of one note. The positive about that is that it lives true to its name and is kid-friendly. But even some kids love more flavor, so those other things are good optional add-ins!

Easy and good. I ended up dissolving the cornstarch in pineapple juice because I started with a bigger can of pineapple. And I used brown sugar - didn't measure but tried to add a little less than a cup.

This is an excellent recipe! And for those of us that can not or do not want sugar in our diets, even we can enjoy. I made it as the original recipe is posted using Apple cider vinegar, but replaced the sugar with granulated Slenda and my family did not even know the difference. I served it over Banquet Popcorn Chicken, Diced orange peppers, pineapple chunks and rice. They loved it.
I have been using this recipe over 3 years, it’s better than some restaurants!

Good recipe! I just used a small can of pineapple juice in place of canned pineapple. So, obviously left out the chunks of pineapple. I thought it was great, adding some red pepper flakes gave it a bit of a kick. This is a keeper!

This Sweet and Sour Chicken Sauce was super simple to make and a great flavor twist on a classic stir fry. If you eat chicken every week and want to try something new, this sauce is it! It's tangy and sweet and the addition of the pineapple and carrots adds texture to a delicious sauce to serve over chicken and rice.

I didn't have high expectations for this thinking it might taste more like sweet ketchup. This is almost restaurant quality and much better than the bottled sauce from the grocery store. Our house asked for it again. I might try to add more vinegar or a bit of chicken stock instead of the water to try to cut the sweetness for our liking. Overall it was a good recipe that we all enjoyed.
that was the best i ever tasted. lasted 3 meals , 2 people
Way too sweet! I'll try it next time with less sugar! My son even thought it was sweet! Overall it was tasty.
The bf loved it ! Making again. Thanks for sharing.

6 1/2 year old approved! My daughter loves the jarred stuff from the grocery store that contains a ton of ingredients. Tonight I made this and didn't tell her. She said it tasted so good and when I told her that it was homemade, she said she liked this even better! I used both the vinegar and the ketchup, and it tasted great! Thanks for sharing this fabulous recipe.

My new favorite sweet and sour chicken recipe. My kids love the sauce. I did make thus before reading the review to not use vinegar and ketchup together. I like it the way you wrote it to post. thanks for sharing this delicious dish :)
